guide.title: Anatomy & Physiology Essentials
guide.lead: You need two things from anatomy on the road: words that everyone understands in your handover, and a mental map of what sits under the spot that hurts. That map tells you which organ may be bleeding or inflamed.

sections.title: Say it precisely
rows: The nose is medial to the eyes
Closer to / farther from the trunk
A cut 10 cm distal to the elbow is on the forearm
The diaphragm is inferior to the lungs
notes: All terms assume the anatomical position: standing, facing forward, palms forward.

groups.title: Left shoulder
items: Spleen or blood under the left diaphragm (Kehr's sign)

sections.title: Body cavities
items: Cranial and spinal: brain and spinal cord
Abdominal and pelvic, separated from the chest by the diaphragm

quiz.q: In the anatomical position, the palms face:
quiz.explanation: All directional terms assume this position.
Lateral is away from the midline.

quiz.q: The transverse plane divides the body into:
The spleen lies in which quadrant?
quiz.explanation: Watch it after blunt left-sided trauma.
Four tissue types: epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous.

quiz.q: Which system includes the brain and spinal cord?
A wound "proximal to the left wrist" is:
options: Between the left wrist and shoulder

quiz.q: Blunt trauma to the left upper quadrant: highest risk organ?
quiz.explanation: Left shoulder pain (Kehr's sign) can accompany splenic bleeding.

quiz.q: Right shoulder pain with right upper quadrant tenderness after a fatty meal suggests:
options: Gallbladder inflammation (referred via the phrenic nerve)
quiz.explanation: Kehr's sign is the left shoulder.
Their pain is often in the back or flank.

flashcards.question: Anatomical position
flashcards.answer: Standing, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms forward. All directional terms refer to it.

flashcards.question: Proximal
flashcards.answer: Closer to the trunk or point of attachment: the shoulder is proximal to the elbow.

flashcards.question: Plane that splits left and right equally
Four quadrants and an organ in each
flashcards.answer: Right upper: liver, gallbladder. Left upper: stomach, spleen. Right lower: appendix. Left lower: sigmoid colon.

flashcards.question: Cavity holding the heart and lungs
flashcards.answer: The thoracic cavity, above the diaphragm.

flashcards.question: System for gas exchange
flashcards.answer: The respiratory system: airways, lungs, diaphragm. It also helps regulate pH.

critical.scenario: Handing over a crash patient, the doctor asks where exactly the forearm cut is. It's on the front of the right forearm, 10 cm below the elbow.
critical.question: How do you describe it?

options.t: 10 cm distal to the right elbow on the anterior forearm
10 cm proximal to the right elbow, lateral forearm
options.f: Below the elbow is distal; the front is anterior.

options.t: 10 cm superior to the right wrist
options.f: Use the closer landmark and the right terms.

critical.explanation: Precise terms prevent errors in handover and documentation.
critical.kpi: Uses correct directional terminology (distal, proximal, anterior, posterior, medial, lateral) in documentation

critical.scenario: A worker fell from a ladder onto his right side: right upper quadrant pain and tenderness over the lower right ribs. BP 100/68, HR 112, no external bleeding.
critical.question: Assessment priority?

options.t: Suspect liver injury with internal bleeding: early shock signs, rapid transport to a trauma centre
Spinal injury is the only concern
options.f: Organ location plus vital signs point to bleeding.
Tachycardia with a soft BP is early shock.

options.t: Give fluids to a normal BP on scene

critical.explanation: The liver is large, vascular and sits behind the lower right ribs.
critical.kpi: Accurately correlates organ location (RUQ=liver) with mechanism of injury to anticipate internal injuries

critical.scenario: A 66-year-old with gallstones has had severe pain for 6 hours after a large meal: worst in the right upper quadrant with guarding, spreading to the right shoulder blade. Temperature 38.4 °C.
critical.question: Which system is most likely involved?

options.t: Biliary: the gallbladder refers pain to the right shoulder via the phrenic nerve

options.f: Stones cause flank pain to the groin.
Kehr's sign is the left shoulder.
Always consider ACS, but this pattern is biliary.

critical.explanation: Guarding means peritoneal irritation; fever suggests infection.
critical.kpi: Applies knowledge of referred pain patterns and organ location to differential assessment
